1	"""Idempotent audit journal of copy/restore operations, with a digest chain.
2	
3	Each journal file records the outcomes of copy and restore operations
4	under caller-chosen idempotency keys. The current sealed format (version
5	2) is ``{"version": 2, "events": {key: [event, previous, digest]},
6	"head": head}`` with ``version``, ``events`` and ``head`` in that order
7	and the events ordered by key code point; every event carries exactly
8	op, target, key, changed, error and stage, in that order. The public
9	order is part of the contract and is verified on read: a document whose
10	root fields, event fields or event keys appear out of order is malformed
11	and raises ``ValueError`` -- it is never reordered and accepted, and a
12	read-only query never rewrites it. ``op`` is ``"copy"`` or ``"restore"``
13	and ``changed`` is a boolean; a successful event has ``error`` and
14	``stage`` both null, while a failed one names the exception class in
15	``error`` and the stage it failed at in ``stage`` -- one of ``"校验"``,
16	``"执行"``, ``"同步"`` and ``"回滚"``.
17	
18	The chain seals every event to its predecessor: each event's digest is
19	the SHA-256 of ``[audit_key, event, previous_digest]`` encoded with the
20	journal's compact UTF-8 JSON convention (compact separators, non-ASCII
21	written through), the first event's previous digest is null, every later
22	one names the digest of the event before it in code-point order, and the
23	root ``head`` carries the last event's digest -- null for an empty
24	journal, so even a tail deletion shows up as an incomplete chain.
25	Digests are sixty-four lowercase hexadecimal digits; anything else is
26	malformed. The older version 1 format (``{"version": 1, "events":
27	{key: event}}``) carries no chain and stays readable: a version 1
28	journal is upgraded to version 2 atomically, old events sealed into the
29	new chain, exactly when :func:`record` appends a new event -- a pure
30	read or an idempotent replay never rewrites it.
31	
32	:func:`record` replays the event already stored under a key: the same
33	key with the same event returns a copy of it together with ``False`` and
34	writes nothing, while the same key with a different event is a conflict
35	and raises ``ValueError``. A new key appends its event -- creating the
36	file when missing, upgrading a version 1 journal, and recomputing the
37	digests of every event from the key's sorted position on -- and returns
38	the event copy together with ``True``. The caller may pass the event's
39	fields in any order -- only the field set must match exactly -- and the
40	event is stored and returned in the public order. :func:`get` is
41	strictly read-only and returns a copy of the event stored under a key;
42	an unknown key raises ``KeyError(key)``.
43	
44	:func:`search` is the read-only paginated query: it scans the journal in
45	ascending audit-key code-point order, keeps only the events at keys
46	strictly greater than an optional exclusive cursor and matching every
47	given filter -- op, failure stage (``"成功"`` selects the successful
48	events) and history key, combined with logical AND -- and returns one
49	page of ``[audit_key, event]`` pairs together with the cursor to resume
50	from, or ``None`` when the page is the last. Non-matching events never
51	consume page capacity.
52	
53	:func:`verify` is the read-only integrity query: it returns ``version``,
54	``count``, ``sealed``, ``valid``, ``first_invalid`` and ``head``, in
55	that order. A well-formed version 1 journal reports its real event count
56	with ``sealed`` and ``valid`` both false and ``first_invalid`` and
57	``head`` both null. A sealed journal whose chain is complete reports
58	``sealed`` and ``valid`` true, ``first_invalid`` null and ``head`` the
59	root digest the file declares. A chain deviation never raises: ``valid``
60	is false and ``first_invalid`` is the zero-based position of the first
61	event whose digest does not match its content or whose predecessor
62	reference is wrong, or the event count when only the root head
63	disagrees. Malformed UTF-8/JSON, an unsupported version or any
64	structural deviation still raises ``ValueError`` here as everywhere.
65	
66	All four functions resolve the journal to its real path and guard the
67	file with a per-realpath lock that excludes both threads of this process
68	and other processes: :func:`record` holds an exclusive kernel flock on
69	the companion lock file (``path + ".lock"``) around the whole
70	validate/replace sequence -- validating the existing chain before
71	appending, so a broken chain raises ``ValueError`` and concurrent
72	inserters serialize, each recomputing its suffix over the complete
73	predecessor document -- and the read-only queries hold a shared one only
74	while opening and reading, so a reader racing a writer observes either
75	the complete previous document or the complete new one -- never a
76	truncated or half-replaced file. The kernel releases the flock on
77	process exit, so a leftover lock file never blocks a later call, and the
78	chain is rebuilt purely from the persisted document, so a restarted
79	process continues from the persisted last event.
80	
81	A record commits via a same-directory temporary file that is written and
82	fsynced, moved over the journal with :func:`os.replace` and followed by
83	a directory fsync. When ``fault`` is ``"replace"`` an ``OSError`` is
84	injected immediately after the replace (before the directory sync),
85	exercising recovery: the journal's pre-call bytes are staged back over
86	it -- or, when the file did not exist beforehand, the new file is
87	removed -- and the directory synced again, all while the exclusive lock
88	is held. If the rollback itself fails, that ``OSError`` is raised with
89	the first error chained as its ``__cause__``. A failure before the
90	replace only discards the temporary. The journal is therefore either the
91	complete pre-call document or the complete post-call one; a failed
92	record never leaves a partially updated file.
93	"""

113	_EVENT_FIELDS = ("op", "target", "key", "changed", "error", "stage")
114	_OPS = ("copy", "restore")
115	_STAGES = ("校验", "执行", "同步", "回滚")
116	# The search stage filter additionally accepts 成功, selecting the
117	# events whose error and stage are both null.

124	def check_pair(audit_path: object, audit_key: object) -> bool:
125	    """Validate the optional ``(audit_path, audit_key)`` argument pair.
126	
127	    Both omitted means auditing is off and returns ``False``; both given
128	    as non-empty strings means auditing and returns ``True``. Exactly one
129	    given, or either value not a non-empty string, is a caller error and
130	    raises ``ValueError`` before the operation starts.
131	    """
132	    if audit_path is None and audit_key is None:
133	        return False
134	    if not isinstance(audit_path, str) or not audit_path \
135	            or not isinstance(audit_key, str) or not audit_key:
136	        raise ValueError(
137	            "audit_path and audit_key must be provided together as "
138	            "non-empty strings")
139	    return True
140	
141	
142	def failure_stage(exc: BaseException) -> str:
143	    """Classify the stage an operation exception leaves the call at.
144	
145	    A target/recovery conflict is ``"执行"``; an :class:`OSError` chained
146	    after the first error by a compensation cleanup or rollback is
147	    ``"回滚"``; argument, history-content, history-key, recovery-copy or
148	    missing-file validation failures (``ValueError``, ``KeyError`` and
149	    ``FileNotFoundError``) are ``"校验"``; every other locking, temporary
150	    file, replace, unlink or fsync failure is ``"同步"``.
151	    """
152	    # The explicit chain (raise ... from first) is the marker of a
153	    # compensation cleanup or rollback that itself failed: the later
154	    # error leaves with the first one as its __cause__ and the stage is
155	    # 回滚, even when that later error happens to be a FileExistsError.
156	    if isinstance(exc, OSError) and exc.__cause__ is not None:
157	        return "回滚"
158	    if isinstance(exc, FileExistsError):
159	        return "执行"
160	    if isinstance(exc, (ValueError, KeyError, FileNotFoundError)):
161	        return "校验"
162	    return "同步"
163	
164	
165	def emit(audit_path: str, audit_key: str, op: str, target: str,
166	         history_key: str, changed: bool,
167	         exc: BaseException | None, stage: str | None) -> Exception | None:
168	    """Append one operation result event, or return the audit's own error.
169	
170	    On success ``exc`` and ``stage`` are ``None``; on failure ``exc`` is
171	    the operation exception (its class name is recorded) and ``stage``
172	    the stage :func:`failure_stage` assigned. Returns ``None`` when the
173	    event was recorded or replayed idempotently, or the journal's own
174	    exception when recording failed so the caller can surface it --
175	    chained after the operation exception when there was one.
176	    """
177	    event = {
178	        "op": op,
179	        "target": target,
180	        "key": history_key,
181	        "changed": bool(changed),
182	        "error": None if exc is None else type(exc).__name__,
183	        "stage": stage,
184	    }
185	    try:
186	        record(audit_path, audit_key, event)
187	    except Exception as audit_exc:  # journal failure: ValueError/OSError/...

214	    # file: flock serializes separate opens of the same lock file across
215	    # processes (and across separate opens in this process), and the
216	    # kernel releases it automatically when the holding process exits --

224	        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
225	        try:
226	            yield
227	        finally:
228	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)

233	def _validate_event(raw: object, *, strict_order: bool) -> dict[str, Any]:
234	    # The field set is part of the contract everywhere; the public field
235	    # order is enforced only for events read from disk. A caller-passed
236	    # event may arrive in any order and is normalized to the public
237	    # order -- never reordered on read, where an out-of-order event is
238	    # malformed and rejected as it stands.
239	    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
240	        raise ValueError("event must be an object with exactly op, target, "
241	                         "key, changed, error and stage")
242	    if strict_order:
243	        if list(raw.keys()) != list(_EVENT_FIELDS):
244	            raise ValueError(
245	                "event fields must be op, target, key, changed, error and "
246	                "stage, in that order")
247	    elif set(raw.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
248	        raise ValueError("event must be an object with exactly op, target, "
249	                         "key, changed, error and stage")
250	    if raw["op"] not in _OPS:
251	        raise ValueError("event op must be copy or restore")
252	    for field in ("target", "key"):
253	        if not isinstance(raw[field], str) or not raw[field]:
254	            raise ValueError(f"event {field} must be a non-empty string")
255	    # bool is checked exactly: ints must not be accepted as booleans.
256	    if not isinstance(raw["changed"], bool):
257	        raise ValueError("event changed must be a boolean")
258	
259	    error = raw["error"]
260	    stage = raw["stage"]
261	    if error is None:
262	        if stage is not None:
263	            raise ValueError("event stage must be null when error is null")
264	    else:
265	        if not isinstance(error, str) or not error:
266	            raise ValueError("event error must be null or a non-empty "
267	                             "exception class name")
268	        if stage not in _STAGES:
269	            raise ValueError(
270	                "event stage must be one of 校验, 执行, 同步, 回滚")
271	    return {field: raw[field] for field in _EVENT_FIELDS}

274	def _is_digest(value: object) -> bool:
275	    # A digest is exactly sixty-four lowercase hexadecimal digits.
276	    return isinstance(value, str) and len(value) == 64 \
277	        and all(char in _HEXADECIMAL for char in value)

280	def _event_digest(audit_key: str, event: dict[str, Any],
281	                  previous: str | None) -> str:
282	    # The digest commits to the audit key, the event and the declared
283	    # predecessor digest, encoded with the journal's compact UTF-8 JSON
284	    # convention: compact separators, non-ASCII written through.
285	    payload = json.dumps([audit_key, event, previous], ensure_ascii=False,
286	                         separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False)
287	    return hashlib.sha256(payload.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

290	def _validate_document(data: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
291	    # The root's public order is part of the contract: an object carrying
292	    # any other set or order of fields is malformed rather than rebuilt.
293	    # Version 1 carries plain events and no chain; version 2 seals every
294	    # event into a [event, previous digest, digest] triple and adds the
295	    # root head.
296	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
297	        raise ValueError("audit root must be an object with keys version "
298	                         "and events, in that order")
299	    root_fields = list(data.keys())
300	    if root_fields == list(_ROOT_FIELDS_V1):
301	        version = 1
302	    elif root_fields == list(_ROOT_FIELDS_V2):
303	        version = 2
304	    else:
305	        raise ValueError("audit root must be an object with keys version "
306	                         "and events, in that order, followed by head in "
307	                         "a sealed journal")
308	
309	    raw_version = data["version"]
310	    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected as a version.
311	    if not isinstance(raw_version, int) or isinstance(raw_version, bool) \
312	            or raw_version != version:
313	        raise ValueError("unsupported audit version")
314	
315	    events_raw = data["events"]
316	    if not isinstance(events_raw, dict):
317	        raise ValueError("events must be an object")
318	
319	    # The persisted form is keyed in code-point order; a document offered
320	    # out of order is malformed and is rejected as it stands -- never
321	    # sorted and accepted, and never rewritten by a read-only query.
322	    event_keys = list(events_raw)
323	    if event_keys != sorted(event_keys):
324	        raise ValueError("audit events must be ordered by key code point")
325	
326	    events: dict[str, Any] = {}
327	    chain: dict[str, Any] = {}
328	    for event_key in event_keys:
329	        if not isinstance(event_key, str) or not event_key:
330	            raise ValueError("event keys must be non-empty strings")
331	        value = events_raw[event_key]
332	        if version == 1:
333	            events[event_key] = _validate_event(value, strict_order=True)
334	            continue
335	        if not isinstance(value, list) or len(value) != 3:
336	            raise ValueError("sealed events must be [event, previous "
337	                             "digest, digest] triples")
338	        event, previous, digest = value
339	        events[event_key] = _validate_event(event, strict_order=True)
340	        if previous is not None and not _is_digest(previous):
341	            raise ValueError("previous digest must be null or a 64-digit "
342	                             "lowercase hexadecimal digest")
343	        if not _is_digest(digest):
344	            raise ValueError("event digest must be a 64-digit lowercase "
345	                             "hexadecimal digest")
346	        chain[event_key] = [previous, digest]
347	
348	    head = None
349	    if version == 2:
350	        head = data["head"]
351	        if head is not None and not _is_digest(head):
352	            raise ValueError("head must be null or a 64-digit lowercase "
353	                             "hexadecimal digest")
354	
355	    return {"version": version, "events": events,
356	            "chain": chain if version == 2 else None, "head": head}
357

359	def _chain_first_invalid(document: dict[str, Any]) -> int | None:
360	    # Zero-based position of the first event whose digest does not match
361	    # its content or whose predecessor reference does not name the digest
362	    # of the event before it; the event count when only the root head
363	    # disagrees with the last event's digest; None when the chain is
364	    # complete. The digest is recomputed over the declared predecessor,
365	    # so a wrong reference surfaces as a broken link at its own position.
366	    events = document["events"]
367	    chain = document["chain"]
368	    previous: str | None = None
369	    for index, event_key in enumerate(events):
370	        declared_previous, digest = chain[event_key]
371	        if digest != _event_digest(event_key, events[event_key],
372	                                   declared_previous):
373	            return index
374	        if declared_previous != previous:
375	            return index
376	        previous = digest
377	    if document["head"] != previous:
378	        return len(events)
379	    return None

382	def _ensure_chain(document: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
383	    # Record and the read-only queries reject a sealed journal whose
384	    # chain is incomplete; only verify reports the deviation instead.
385	    if document["version"] == 2 \
386	            and _chain_first_invalid(document) is not None:
387	        raise ValueError("audit digest chain is incomplete")

404	def _read_document(
405	    realpath: str,
406	) -> tuple[dict[str, Any] | None, bytes | None]:
407	    # The journal is created on demand, so a missing file simply means no
408	    # event has been recorded yet; the raw bytes are returned as well so a
409	    # later rollback can restore that exact pre-call content.
410	    try:
411	        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
412	            raw = handle.read()
413	    except FileNotFoundError:
414	        return None, None
415	
416	    document = _parse_document(realpath, raw)
417	    _ensure_chain(document)
418	    return document, raw

421	def _serialize(chain: dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
422	    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, events ordered by key
423	    # code point, terminated by exactly one newline. ``chain`` maps each
424	    # audit key to its [event, previous digest, digest] triple; the root
425	    # head carries the last event's digest, null for an empty journal.
426	    ordered = {key: chain[key] for key in sorted(chain)}
427	    head = ordered[list(ordered)[-1]][2] if ordered else None
428	    document = {"version": _VERSION, "events": ordered, "head": head}
429	    text = json.dumps(document, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
430	                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
431	    return text.encode("utf-8")

442	def _rollback(
443	    realpath: str,
444	    directory: str,
445	    old_bytes: bytes | None,
446	    first: BaseException,
447	) -> None:
448	    # Restore the exact state the journal held when record started, while
449	    # the exclusive lock is still held: stage the pre-call bytes back over
450	    # the replaced file (same-directory temporary, fsync, replace), or
451	    # remove the file when it did not exist beforehand; sync the directory
452	    # afterwards. Any failure of this recovery is raised chained after the
453	    # first error.
454	    try:
455	        if old_bytes is None:
456	            try:
457	                os.unlink(realpath)
458	            except FileNotFoundError:
459	                pass
460	        else:
461	            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
462	                dir=directory, prefix=".audit-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
463	            try:
464	                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
465	                    handle.write(old_bytes)
466	                    handle.flush()
467	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
468	                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
469	            except BaseException:
470	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
471	                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
472	                raise
473	        _fsync_dir(directory)
474	    except OSError as recovery:
475	        raise recovery from first

478	def _commit(
479	    realpath: str,
480	    directory: str,
481	    payload: bytes,
482	    old_bytes: bytes | None,
483	    fault: str | None,
484	) -> None:
485	    # Phase 1: stage the new bytes in a same-directory temporary, fsync
486	    # them, then atomically move them over the journal. Until the replace
487	    # succeeds the journal still holds the pre-call bytes, so a failure
488	    # only removes this attempt's temporary.
489	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
490	        dir=directory, prefix=".audit-", suffix=".tmp")
491	    try:
492	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
493	            handle.write(payload)
494	            handle.flush()
495	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
496	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
497	    except BaseException as first:
498	        try:
499	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
500	        except FileNotFoundError:
501	            pass
502	        except OSError as cleanup:
503	            raise cleanup from first
504	        raise
505	
506	    # Phase 2: persist the replace with a directory fsync. The journal has
507	    # already been replaced at this point, so any failure -- the injected
508	    # "replace" fault included -- must restore the pre-call bytes (or the
509	    # file's prior nonexistence) while the lock is held.
510	    try:
511	        if fault == "replace":
512	            raise OSError("injected failure after audit file replace")
513	        _fsync_dir(directory)
514	    except BaseException as first:
515	        _rollback(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
516	        raise

519	def record(
520	    path: str,
521	    key: str,
522	    event: dict[str, Any],
523	    fault: str | None = None,
524	) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], bool]:
525	    """Record one copy/restore audit event under an idempotency ``key``.
526	
527	    ``path`` and ``key`` must be non-empty strings and ``event`` an object
528	    with exactly op, target, key, changed, error and stage -- in any
529	    order; the event is stored and returned in the public order. ``op``
530	    must be ``"copy"`` or ``"restore"``, ``target`` and the event's own
531	    ``key`` non-empty strings and ``changed`` a boolean. On success
532	    ``error`` and ``stage`` must both be null; on failure ``error`` must
533	    be a non-empty exception class name and ``stage`` one of ``"校验"``,
534	    ``"执行"``, ``"同步"`` and ``"回滚"``. Any invalid input raises
535	    ``ValueError``, and so does ``fault`` being anything other than
536	    ``None`` or ``"replace"``.
537	
538	    Returns ``(event, created)``: ``True`` when this call appended the
539	    event (creating the journal file if missing), ``False`` when the key
540	    already carried an identical event -- that replay writes nothing and
541	    never triggers the ``fault``. A key already carrying a different event
542	    raises ``ValueError``. A missing parent directory raises
543	    ``FileNotFoundError``; malformed JSON or UTF-8, a negative-zero
544	    literal, an unsupported version or structure, or an incomplete digest
545	    chain in an existing journal raises ``ValueError``; any other locking
546	    or I/O failure raises ``OSError``.
547	
548	    The append seals the event into the digest chain: a version 1
549	    journal is upgraded to version 2 atomically with the same commit,
550	    its old events sealed alongside the new one, and a key landing
551	    between existing ones has every digest from its sorted position on
552	    recomputed. The existing chain is validated under the exclusive lock
553	    before anything is written, so concurrent inserters serialize and
554	    each extends a complete predecessor document.
555	
556	    The commit writes a same-directory temporary, fsyncs it, replaces the
557	    journal atomically and fsyncs its directory. With
558	    ``fault="replace"`` an ``OSError`` is raised right after the replace;
559	    the call then restores the journal's pre-call bytes, or removes the
560	    newly created file, before propagating it -- chained after the first
561	    error should the rollback itself fail.
562	    """
563	    for value in (path, key):
564	        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
565	            raise ValueError("path and key must be non-empty strings")
566	    clean_event = _validate_event(event, strict_order=False)
567	    if fault is not None and fault != "replace":
568	        raise ValueError('fault must be None or "replace"')
569	
570	    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
571	    store = _get_store(realpath)
572	    with store.lock:
573	        with _file_lock(realpath):
574	            document, old_bytes = _read_document(realpath)
575	            events: dict[str, Any] = (
576	                {} if document is None else dict(document["events"]))
577	
578	            existing = events.get(key)
579	            if existing is not None:
580	                if existing != clean_event:
581	                    raise ValueError(
582	                        "audit key was already used with a different event")
583	                return dict(existing), False
584	
585	            events[key] = clean_event
586	            # Seal the whole sorted key sequence: a key landing between
587	            # existing ones changes its successor's predecessor, so every
588	            # digest from the insertion point on is recomputed -- earlier
589	            # ones recompute to themselves. A version 1 journal is
590	            # upgraded by the same commit, its old events sealed into the
591	            # new chain.
592	            chain: dict[str, Any] = {}
593	            previous: str | None = None
594	            for event_key in sorted(events):
595	                digest = _event_digest(event_key, events[event_key],
596	                                       previous)
597	                chain[event_key] = [events[event_key], previous, digest]
598	                previous = digest
599	            directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
600	            _commit(realpath, directory, _serialize(chain), old_bytes,
601	                    fault)
602	            return dict(clean_event), True
603

605	def _read_existing_document(realpath: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
606	    # Read-only path shared by get and search: the shared flock is held
607	    # only while the file is opened and read, so a query racing a writer
608	    # observes either the complete previous document or the complete new
609	    # one. A missing journal surfaces as FileNotFoundError; malformed
610	    # UTF-8/JSON (negative-zero literals included), an unsupported
611	    # version, any structural or order deviation, or an incomplete digest
612	    # chain raises ValueError -- the document is never reordered and
613	    # accepted, and never rewritten.
614	    with _file_lock(realpath, shared=True):
615	        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
616	            raw = handle.read()
617	
618	    document = _parse_document(realpath, raw)
619	    _ensure_chain(document)
620	    return document

623	def get(path: str, key: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
624	    """Return a read-only copy of the audit event stored under ``key``.
625	
626	    ``path`` and ``key`` must be non-empty strings, else ``ValueError``.
627	    A missing journal file raises ``FileNotFoundError``; malformed JSON or
628	    UTF-8, a negative-zero literal, an unsupported version or structure,
629	    or an incomplete digest chain raises ``ValueError``; an unknown key
630	    raises ``KeyError(key)``; any other locking or I/O failure raises
631	    ``OSError``. The query never writes and holds the journal's companion
632	    lock shared only while the file is opened and read, so it can only
633	    observe a complete document. The returned dict is a fresh copy with
634	    fields op, target, key, changed, error and stage in that order;
635	    mutating it never affects the journal.
636	    """
637	    for value in (path, key):
638	        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
639	            raise ValueError("path and key must be non-empty strings")
640	
641	    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
642	    document = _read_existing_document(realpath)
643	
644	    events = document["events"]
645	    if key not in events:
646	        raise KeyError(key)
647	    return dict(events[key])

650	def _matches(event: dict[str, Any], op: str | None, stage: str | None,
651	             key: str | None) -> bool:
652	    # Every provided filter must hold (logical AND). "成功" selects the
653	    # successful events -- error and stage both null -- while any other
654	    # stage filter names the failure stage to match exactly. The history
655	    # key filter is a plain string equality: no prefix matching, case
656	    # folding or path normalization.
657	    if op is not None and event["op"] != op:
658	        return False
659	    if stage is not None:
660	        if stage == "成功":
661	            if event["error"] is not None or event["stage"] is not None:
662	                return False
663	        elif event["stage"] != stage:
664	            return False
665	    if key is not None and event["key"] != key:
666	        return False
667	    return True

670	def search(
671	    path: str,
672	    cursor: str | None = None,
673	    limit: int = _DEFAULT_LIMIT,
674	    op: str | None = None,
675	    stage: str | None = None,
676	    key: str | None = None,
677	) -> dict[str, Any]:
678	    """Return one page of audit events matching the given filters.
679	
680	    ``path`` must be a non-empty string. ``cursor`` is ``None`` or a
681	    non-empty string -- it need not name an existing event -- and only
682	    events whose audit key is strictly greater than it in code-point
683	    order are considered. ``limit`` is the page size: an integer from 1
684	    to 1000 (booleans are rejected), defaulting to 100. Each of ``op``,
685	    ``stage`` and ``key`` is an optional filter; all given filters must
686	    hold simultaneously. ``op`` is ``"copy"`` or ``"restore"``; ``stage``
687	    is one of ``"成功"`` (events whose error and stage are both null),
688	    ``"校验"``, ``"执行"``, ``"同步"`` and ``"回滚"`` (events that failed
689	    at that stage); ``key`` matches the event's history key by exact
690	    string equality. Any other value raises ``ValueError``.
691	
692	    The journal is scanned in ascending audit-key code-point order and
693	    filtered afterwards, so non-matching events never consume page
694	    capacity. Returns ``{"events": [[audit_key, event], ...], "next":
695	    cursor_or_none}``: each event is a fresh copy with the public field
696	    order, and ``next`` is the audit key of the page's last item when
697	    further matching events remain, else ``None``. With no matching
698	    events the page is empty and ``next`` is ``None``.
699	
700	    The query is strictly read-only: a missing journal raises
701	    ``FileNotFoundError``; malformed JSON or UTF-8, a negative-zero
702	    literal, or an unsupported version, structure, order or digest chain
703	    raises ``ValueError``; any other locking or I/O failure raises
704	    ``OSError``. It holds the journal's companion lock shared only while
705	    the file is opened and read, so a query racing a writer observes
706	    either the complete previous document or the complete new one.
707	    """
708	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
709	        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
710	    if cursor is not None and (not isinstance(cursor, str) or not cursor):
711	        raise ValueError("cursor must be None or a non-empty string")
712	    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected as a page size.
713	    if not isinstance(limit, int) or isinstance(limit, bool) \
714	            or not 1 <= limit <= _MAX_LIMIT:
715	        raise ValueError("limit must be an integer between 1 and 1000")
716	    if op is not None and op not in _OPS:
717	        raise ValueError('op filter must be "copy" or "restore"')
718	    if stage is not None and stage not in _SEARCH_STAGES:
719	        raise ValueError(
720	            "stage filter must be one of 成功, 校验, 执行, 同步, 回滚")
721	    if key is not None and (not isinstance(key, str) or not key):
722	        raise ValueError("key filter must be a non-empty string")
723	
724	    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
725	    document = _read_existing_document(realpath)
726	
727	    # The persisted events are validated to be in ascending key
728	    # code-point order, so the document order is the scan order. One
729	    # extra match is collected to learn whether the page is the last.
730	    matches: list[list[Any]] = []
731	    for audit_key, event in document["events"].items():
732	        if cursor is not None and audit_key <= cursor:
733	            continue
734	        if not _matches(event, op, stage, key):
735	            continue
736	        matches.append([audit_key, dict(event)])
737	        if len(matches) > limit:
738	            break
739	
740	    if len(matches) > limit:
741	        page = matches[:limit]
742	        next_cursor: str | None = page[-1][0]
743	    else:
744	        page = matches
745	        next_cursor = None
746	    return {"events": page, "next": next_cursor}

749	def verify(path: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
750	    """Verify the integrity of the audit journal stored at ``path``.
751	
752	    ``path`` must be a non-empty string, else ``ValueError``. A missing
753	    journal raises ``FileNotFoundError``; malformed JSON or UTF-8, a
754	    negative-zero literal, or an unsupported version, field order or
755	    structure raises ``ValueError``; any other locking or I/O failure
756	    raises ``OSError``. The query never writes and holds the journal's
757	    companion lock shared only while the file is opened and read.
758	
759	    Returns ``version``, ``count``, ``sealed``, ``valid``,
760	    ``first_invalid`` and ``head``, in that order. A well-formed version
761	    1 journal carries no chain: ``count`` is its real event count,
762	    ``sealed`` and ``valid`` are false and ``first_invalid`` and
763	    ``head`` are null. A sealed (version 2) journal whose chain is
764	    complete reports ``sealed`` and ``valid`` true, ``first_invalid``
765	    null and ``head`` the root digest the file declares. A chain
766	    deviation never raises: ``valid`` is false and ``first_invalid`` is
767	    the zero-based position of the first event whose digest does not
768	    match its content or whose predecessor reference is wrong, or the
769	    event count when only the root head disagrees with the last event's
770	    digest.
771	    """
772	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:

"""Idempotent audit journal of copy/restore operations, with a digest chain.

Each journal file records the outcomes of copy and restore operations
under caller-chosen idempotency keys. The current sealed format (version
2) is ``{"version": 2, "events": {key: [event, previous, digest]},
"head": head}`` with ``version``, ``events`` and ``head`` in that order
and the events ordered by key code point; every event carries exactly
op, target, key, changed, error and stage, in that order. The public
order is part of the contract and is verified on read: a document whose
root fields, event fields or event keys appear out of order is malformed
and raises ``ValueError`` -- it is never reordered and accepted, and a
read-only query never rewrites it. ``op`` is ``"copy"`` or ``"restore"``
and ``changed`` is a boolean; a successful event has ``error`` and
``stage`` both null, while a failed one names the exception class in
``error`` and the stage it failed at in ``stage`` -- one of ``"校验"``,
``"执行"``, ``"同步"`` and ``"回滚"``.

The chain seals every event to its predecessor: each event's digest is
the SHA-256 of ``[audit_key, event, previous_digest]`` encoded with the
journal's compact UTF-8 JSON convention (compact separators, non-ASCII
written through), the first event's previous digest is null, every later
one names the digest of the event before it in code-point order, and the
root ``head`` carries the last event's digest -- null for an empty
journal, so even a tail deletion shows up as an incomplete chain.
Digests are sixty-four lowercase hexadecimal digits; anything else is
malformed. The older version 1 format (``{"version": 1, "events":
{key: event}}``) carries no chain and stays readable: a version 1
journal is upgraded to version 2 atomically, old events sealed into the
new chain, exactly when :func:`record` appends a new event -- a pure
read or an idempotent replay never rewrites it.

:func:`record` replays the event already stored under a key: the same
key with the same event returns a copy of it together with ``False`` and
writes nothing, while the same key with a different event is a conflict
and raises ``ValueError``. A new key appends its event -- creating the
file when missing, upgrading a version 1 journal, and recomputing the
digests of every event from the key's sorted position on -- and returns
the event copy together with ``True``. The caller may pass the event's
fields in any order -- only the field set must match exactly -- and the
event is stored and returned in the public order. :func:`get` is
strictly read-only and returns a copy of the event stored under a key;
an unknown key raises ``KeyError(key)``.

:func:`search` is the read-only paginated query: it scans the journal in
ascending audit-key code-point order, keeps only the events at keys
strictly greater than an optional exclusive cursor and matching every
given filter -- op, failure stage (``"成功"`` selects the successful
events) and history key, combined with logical AND -- and returns one
page of ``[audit_key, event]`` pairs together with the cursor to resume
from, or ``None`` when the page is the last. Non-matching events never
consume page capacity.

:func:`verify` is the read-only integrity query: it returns ``version``,
``count``, ``sealed``, ``valid``, ``first_invalid`` and ``head``, in
that order. A well-formed version 1 journal reports its real event count
with ``sealed`` and ``valid`` both false and ``first_invalid`` and
``head`` both null. A sealed journal whose chain is complete reports
``sealed`` and ``valid`` true, ``first_invalid`` null and ``head`` the
root digest the file declares. A chain deviation never raises: ``valid``
is false and ``first_invalid`` is the zero-based position of the first
event whose digest does not match its content or whose predecessor
reference is wrong, or the event count when only the root head
disagrees. Malformed UTF-8/JSON, an unsupported version or any
structural deviation still raises ``ValueError`` here as everywhere.

All four functions resolve the journal to its real path and guard the
file with a per-realpath lock that excludes both threads of this process
and other processes: :func:`record` holds an exclusive kernel flock on
the companion lock file (``path + ".lock"``) around the whole
validate/replace sequence -- validating the existing chain before
appending, so a broken chain raises ``ValueError`` and concurrent
inserters serialize, each recomputing its suffix over the complete
predecessor document -- and the read-only queries hold a shared one only
while opening and reading, so a reader racing a writer observes either
the complete previous document or the complete new one -- never a
truncated or half-replaced file. The kernel releases the flock on
process exit, so a leftover lock file never blocks a later call, and the
chain is rebuilt purely from the persisted document, so a restarted
process continues from the persisted last event.

A record commits via a same-directory temporary file that is written and
fsynced, moved over the journal with :func:`os.replace` and followed by
a directory fsync. When ``fault`` is ``"replace"`` an ``OSError`` is
injected immediately after the replace (before the directory sync),
exercising recovery: the journal's pre-call bytes are staged back over
it -- or, when the file did not exist beforehand, the new file is
removed -- and the directory synced again, all while the exclusive lock
is held. If the rollback itself fails, that ``OSError`` is raised with
the first error chained as its ``__cause__``. A failure before the
replace only discards the temporary. The journal is therefore either the
complete pre-call document or the complete post-call one; a failed
record never leaves a partially updated file.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import fcntl
import hashlib
import json
import os
import tempfile
import threading
from typing import Any, Iterator

from ._jsonio import strict_loads

__all__ = ["record", "get", "search", "verify"]

_VERSION = 2
_ROOT_FIELDS_V1 = ("version", "events")
_ROOT_FIELDS_V2 = ("version", "events", "head")
_EVENT_FIELDS = ("op", "target", "key", "changed", "error", "stage")
_OPS = ("copy", "restore")
_STAGES = ("校验", "执行", "同步", "回滚")
# The search stage filter additionally accepts 成功, selecting the
# events whose error and stage are both null.
_SEARCH_STAGES = ("成功",) + _STAGES
_DEFAULT_LIMIT = 100
_MAX_LIMIT = 1000
_HEXADECIMAL = frozenset("0123456789abcdef")


def check_pair(audit_path: object, audit_key: object) -> bool:
    """Validate the optional ``(audit_path, audit_key)`` argument pair.

    Both omitted means auditing is off and returns ``False``; both given
    as non-empty strings means auditing and returns ``True``. Exactly one
    given, or either value not a non-empty string, is a caller error and
    raises ``ValueError`` before the operation starts.
    """
    if audit_path is None and audit_key is None:
        return False
    if not isinstance(audit_path, str) or not audit_path \
            or not isinstance(audit_key, str) or not audit_key:
        raise ValueError(
            "audit_path and audit_key must be provided together as "
            "non-empty strings")
    return True


def failure_stage(exc: BaseException) -> str:
    """Classify the stage an operation exception leaves the call at.

    A target/recovery conflict is ``"执行"``; an :class:`OSError` chained
    after the first error by a compensation cleanup or rollback is
    ``"回滚"``; argument, history-content, history-key, recovery-copy or
    missing-file validation failures (``ValueError``, ``KeyError`` and
    ``FileNotFoundError``) are ``"校验"``; every other locking, temporary
    file, replace, unlink or fsync failure is ``"同步"``.
    """
    # The explicit chain (raise ... from first) is the marker of a
    # compensation cleanup or rollback that itself failed: the later
    # error leaves with the first one as its __cause__ and the stage is
    # 回滚, even when that later error happens to be a FileExistsError.
    if isinstance(exc, OSError) and exc.__cause__ is not None:
        return "回滚"
    if isinstance(exc, FileExistsError):
        return "执行"
    if isinstance(exc, (ValueError, KeyError, FileNotFoundError)):
        return "校验"
    return "同步"


def emit(audit_path: str, audit_key: str, op: str, target: str,
         history_key: str, changed: bool,
         exc: BaseException | None, stage: str | None) -> Exception | None:
    """Append one operation result event, or return the audit's own error.

    On success ``exc`` and ``stage`` are ``None``; on failure ``exc`` is
    the operation exception (its class name is recorded) and ``stage``
    the stage :func:`failure_stage` assigned. Returns ``None`` when the
    event was recorded or replayed idempotently, or the journal's own
    exception when recording failed so the caller can surface it --
    chained after the operation exception when there was one.
    """
    event = {
        "op": op,
        "target": target,
        "key": history_key,
        "changed": bool(changed),
        "error": None if exc is None else type(exc).__name__,
        "stage": stage,
    }
    try:
        record(audit_path, audit_key, event)
    except Exception as audit_exc:  # journal failure: ValueError/OSError/...
        return audit_exc
    return None


class _Store:
    def __init__(self, realpath: str) -> None:
        self.realpath = realpath
        self.lock = threading.Lock()


_stores_lock = threading.Lock()
_stores: dict[str, _Store] = {}


def _get_store(realpath: str) -> _Store:
    with _stores_lock:
        store = _stores.get(realpath)
        if store is None:
            store = _Store(realpath)
            _stores[realpath] = store
        return store


@contextlib.contextmanager
def _file_lock(realpath: str, *, shared: bool = False) -> Iterator[None]:
    # Cross-process exclusion via a kernel flock on the companion lock
    # file: flock serializes separate opens of the same lock file across
    # processes (and across separate opens in this process), and the
    # kernel releases it automatically when the holding process exits --
    # even on a crash -- so a leftover lock file never blocks anyone. The
    # file is deliberately never unlinked: removing it while another
    # process waits on the old inode would split the lock domain. Any
    # failure to open or lock surfaces unchanged as OSError.
    lock_path = realpath + ".lock"
    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
    try:
        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def _validate_event(raw: object, *, strict_order: bool) -> dict[str, Any]:
    # The field set is part of the contract everywhere; the public field
    # order is enforced only for events read from disk. A caller-passed
    # event may arrive in any order and is normalized to the public
    # order -- never reordered on read, where an out-of-order event is
    # malformed and rejected as it stands.
    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
        raise ValueError("event must be an object with exactly op, target, "
                         "key, changed, error and stage")
    if strict_order:
        if list(raw.keys()) != list(_EVENT_FIELDS):
            raise ValueError(
                "event fields must be op, target, key, changed, error and "
                "stage, in that order")
    elif set(raw.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("event must be an object with exactly op, target, "
                         "key, changed, error and stage")
    if raw["op"] not in _OPS:
        raise ValueError("event op must be copy or restore")
    for field in ("target", "key"):
        if not isinstance(raw[field], str) or not raw[field]:
            raise ValueError(f"event {field} must be a non-empty string")
    # bool is checked exactly: ints must not be accepted as booleans.
    if not isinstance(raw["changed"], bool):
        raise ValueError("event changed must be a boolean")

    error = raw["error"]
    stage = raw["stage"]
    if error is None:
        if stage is not None:
            raise ValueError("event stage must be null when error is null")
    else:
        if not isinstance(error, str) or not error:
            raise ValueError("event error must be null or a non-empty "
                             "exception class name")
        if stage not in _STAGES:
            raise ValueError(
                "event stage must be one of 校验, 执行, 同步, 回滚")
    return {field: raw[field] for field in _EVENT_FIELDS}


def _is_digest(value: object) -> bool:
    # A digest is exactly sixty-four lowercase hexadecimal digits.
    return isinstance(value, str) and len(value) == 64 \
        and all(char in _HEXADECIMAL for char in value)


def _event_digest(audit_key: str, event: dict[str, Any],
                  previous: str | None) -> str:
    # The digest commits to the audit key, the event and the declared
    # predecessor digest, encoded with the journal's compact UTF-8 JSON
    # convention: compact separators, non-ASCII written through.
    payload = json.dumps([audit_key, event, previous], ensure_ascii=False,
                         separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False)
    return hashlib.sha256(payload.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def _validate_document(data: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
    # The root's public order is part of the contract: an object carrying
    # any other set or order of fields is malformed rather than rebuilt.
    # Version 1 carries plain events and no chain; version 2 seals every
    # event into a [event, previous digest, digest] triple and adds the
    # root head.
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise ValueError("audit root must be an object with keys version "
                         "and events, in that order")
    root_fields = list(data.keys())
    if root_fields == list(_ROOT_FIELDS_V1):
        version = 1
    elif root_fields == list(_ROOT_FIELDS_V2):
        version = 2
    else:
        raise ValueError("audit root must be an object with keys version "
                         "and events, in that order, followed by head in "
                         "a sealed journal")

    raw_version = data["version"]
    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected as a version.
    if not isinstance(raw_version, int) or isinstance(raw_version, bool) \
            or raw_version != version:
        raise ValueError("unsupported audit version")

    events_raw = data["events"]
    if not isinstance(events_raw, dict):
        raise ValueError("events must be an object")

    # The persisted form is keyed in code-point order; a document offered
    # out of order is malformed and is rejected as it stands -- never
    # sorted and accepted, and never rewritten by a read-only query.
    event_keys = list(events_raw)
    if event_keys != sorted(event_keys):
        raise ValueError("audit events must be ordered by key code point")

    events: dict[str, Any] = {}
    chain: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for event_key in event_keys:
        if not isinstance(event_key, str) or not event_key:
            raise ValueError("event keys must be non-empty strings")
        value = events_raw[event_key]
        if version == 1:
            events[event_key] = _validate_event(value, strict_order=True)
            continue
        if not isinstance(value, list) or len(value) != 3:
            raise ValueError("sealed events must be [event, previous "
                             "digest, digest] triples")
        event, previous, digest = value
        events[event_key] = _validate_event(event, strict_order=True)
        if previous is not None and not _is_digest(previous):
            raise ValueError("previous digest must be null or a 64-digit "
                             "lowercase hexadecimal digest")
        if not _is_digest(digest):
            raise ValueError("event digest must be a 64-digit lowercase "
                             "hexadecimal digest")
        chain[event_key] = [previous, digest]

    head = None
    if version == 2:
        head = data["head"]
        if head is not None and not _is_digest(head):
            raise ValueError("head must be null or a 64-digit lowercase "
                             "hexadecimal digest")

    return {"version": version, "events": events,
            "chain": chain if version == 2 else None, "head": head}


def _chain_first_invalid(document: dict[str, Any]) -> int | None:
    # Zero-based position of the first event whose digest does not match
    # its content or whose predecessor reference does not name the digest
    # of the event before it; the event count when only the root head
    # disagrees with the last event's digest; None when the chain is
    # complete. The digest is recomputed over the declared predecessor,
    # so a wrong reference surfaces as a broken link at its own position.
    events = document["events"]
    chain = document["chain"]
    previous: str | None = None
    for index, event_key in enumerate(events):
        declared_previous, digest = chain[event_key]
        if digest != _event_digest(event_key, events[event_key],
                                   declared_previous):
            return index
        if declared_previous != previous:
            return index
        previous = digest
    if document["head"] != previous:
        return len(events)
    return None


def _ensure_chain(document: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    # Record and the read-only queries reject a sealed journal whose
    # chain is incomplete; only verify reports the deviation instead.
    if document["version"] == 2 \
            and _chain_first_invalid(document) is not None:
        raise ValueError("audit digest chain is incomplete")


def _parse_document(realpath: str, raw: bytes) -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"audit file {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
    try:
        data = strict_loads(text)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"audit file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
    return _validate_document(data)


def _read_document(
    realpath: str,
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any] | None, bytes | None]:
    # The journal is created on demand, so a missing file simply means no
    # event has been recorded yet; the raw bytes are returned as well so a
    # later rollback can restore that exact pre-call content.
    try:
        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None, None

    document = _parse_document(realpath, raw)
    _ensure_chain(document)
    return document, raw


def _serialize(chain: dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, events ordered by key
    # code point, terminated by exactly one newline. ``chain`` maps each
    # audit key to its [event, previous digest, digest] triple; the root
    # head carries the last event's digest, null for an empty journal.
    ordered = {key: chain[key] for key in sorted(chain)}
    head = ordered[list(ordered)[-1]][2] if ordered else None
    document = {"version": _VERSION, "events": ordered, "head": head}
    text = json.dumps(document, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
    return text.encode("utf-8")


def _fsync_dir(directory: str) -> None:
    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.fsync(dir_fd)
    finally:
        os.close(dir_fd)


def _rollback(
    realpath: str,
    directory: str,
    old_bytes: bytes | None,
    first: BaseException,
) -> None:
    # Restore the exact state the journal held when record started, while
    # the exclusive lock is still held: stage the pre-call bytes back over
    # the replaced file (same-directory temporary, fsync, replace), or
    # remove the file when it did not exist beforehand; sync the directory
    # afterwards. Any failure of this recovery is raised chained after the
    # first error.
    try:
        if old_bytes is None:
            try:
                os.unlink(realpath)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
        else:
            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
                dir=directory, prefix=".audit-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
            try:
                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
                    handle.write(old_bytes)
                    handle.flush()
                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
            except BaseException:
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
                raise
        _fsync_dir(directory)
    except OSError as recovery:
        raise recovery from first


def _commit(
    realpath: str,
    directory: str,
    payload: bytes,
    old_bytes: bytes | None,
    fault: str | None,
) -> None:
    # Phase 1: stage the new bytes in a same-directory temporary, fsync
    # them, then atomically move them over the journal. Until the replace
    # succeeds the journal still holds the pre-call bytes, so a failure
    # only removes this attempt's temporary.
    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
        dir=directory, prefix=".audit-", suffix=".tmp")
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(payload)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
    except BaseException as first:
        try:
            os.unlink(tmp_path)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            pass
        except OSError as cleanup:
            raise cleanup from first
        raise

    # Phase 2: persist the replace with a directory fsync. The journal has
    # already been replaced at this point, so any failure -- the injected
    # "replace" fault included -- must restore the pre-call bytes (or the
    # file's prior nonexistence) while the lock is held.
    try:
        if fault == "replace":
            raise OSError("injected failure after audit file replace")
        _fsync_dir(directory)
    except BaseException as first:
        _rollback(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
        raise


def record(
    path: str,
    key: str,
    event: dict[str, Any],
    fault: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], bool]:
    """Record one copy/restore audit event under an idempotency ``key``.

    ``path`` and ``key`` must be non-empty strings and ``event`` an object
    with exactly op, target, key, changed, error and stage -- in any
    order; the event is stored and returned in the public order. ``op``
    must be ``"copy"`` or ``"restore"``, ``target`` and the event's own
    ``key`` non-empty strings and ``changed`` a boolean. On success
    ``error`` and ``stage`` must both be null; on failure ``error`` must
    be a non-empty exception class name and ``stage`` one of ``"校验"``,
    ``"执行"``, ``"同步"`` and ``"回滚"``. Any invalid input raises
    ``ValueError``, and so does ``fault`` being anything other than
    ``None`` or ``"replace"``.

    Returns ``(event, created)``: ``True`` when this call appended the
    event (creating the journal file if missing), ``False`` when the key
    already carried an identical event -- that replay writes nothing and
    never triggers the ``fault``. A key already carrying a different event
    raises ``ValueError``. A missing parent directory raises
    ``FileNotFoundError``; malformed JSON or UTF-8, a negative-zero
    literal, an unsupported version or structure, or an incomplete digest
    chain in an existing journal raises ``ValueError``; any other locking
    or I/O failure raises ``OSError``.

    The append seals the event into the digest chain: a version 1
    journal is upgraded to version 2 atomically with the same commit,
    its old events sealed alongside the new one, and a key landing
    between existing ones has every digest from its sorted position on
    recomputed. The existing chain is validated under the exclusive lock
    before anything is written, so concurrent inserters serialize and
    each extends a complete predecessor document.

    The commit writes a same-directory temporary, fsyncs it, replaces the
    journal atomically and fsyncs its directory. With
    ``fault="replace"`` an ``OSError`` is raised right after the replace;
    the call then restores the journal's pre-call bytes, or removes the
    newly created file, before propagating it -- chained after the first
    error should the rollback itself fail.
    """
    for value in (path, key):
        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
            raise ValueError("path and key must be non-empty strings")
    clean_event = _validate_event(event, strict_order=False)
    if fault is not None and fault != "replace":
        raise ValueError('fault must be None or "replace"')

    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
    store = _get_store(realpath)
    with store.lock:
        with _file_lock(realpath):
            document, old_bytes = _read_document(realpath)
            events: dict[str, Any] = (
                {} if document is None else dict(document["events"]))

            existing = events.get(key)
            if existing is not None:
                if existing != clean_event:
                    raise ValueError(
                        "audit key was already used with a different event")
                return dict(existing), False

            events[key] = clean_event
            # Seal the whole sorted key sequence: a key landing between
            # existing ones changes its successor's predecessor, so every
            # digest from the insertion point on is recomputed -- earlier
            # ones recompute to themselves. A version 1 journal is
            # upgraded by the same commit, its old events sealed into the
            # new chain.
            chain: dict[str, Any] = {}
            previous: str | None = None
            for event_key in sorted(events):
                digest = _event_digest(event_key, events[event_key],
                                       previous)
                chain[event_key] = [events[event_key], previous, digest]
                previous = digest
            directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
            _commit(realpath, directory, _serialize(chain), old_bytes,
                    fault)
            return dict(clean_event), True


def _read_existing_document(realpath: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    # Read-only path shared by get and search: the shared flock is held
    # only while the file is opened and read, so a query racing a writer
    # observes either the complete previous document or the complete new
    # one. A missing journal surfaces as FileNotFoundError; malformed
    # UTF-8/JSON (negative-zero literals included), an unsupported
    # version, any structural or order deviation, or an incomplete digest
    # chain raises ValueError -- the document is never reordered and
    # accepted, and never rewritten.
    with _file_lock(realpath, shared=True):
        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()

    document = _parse_document(realpath, raw)
    _ensure_chain(document)
    return document


def get(path: str, key: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return a read-only copy of the audit event stored under ``key``.

    ``path`` and ``key`` must be non-empty strings, else ``ValueError``.
    A missing journal file raises ``FileNotFoundError``; malformed JSON or
    UTF-8, a negative-zero literal, an unsupported version or structure,
    or an incomplete digest chain raises ``ValueError``; an unknown key
    raises ``KeyError(key)``; any other locking or I/O failure raises
    ``OSError``. The query never writes and holds the journal's companion
    lock shared only while the file is opened and read, so it can only
    observe a complete document. The returned dict is a fresh copy with
    fields op, target, key, changed, error and stage in that order;
    mutating it never affects the journal.
    """
    for value in (path, key):
        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
            raise ValueError("path and key must be non-empty strings")

    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
    document = _read_existing_document(realpath)

    events = document["events"]
    if key not in events:
        raise KeyError(key)
    return dict(events[key])


def _matches(event: dict[str, Any], op: str | None, stage: str | None,
             key: str | None) -> bool:
    # Every provided filter must hold (logical AND). "成功" selects the
    # successful events -- error and stage both null -- while any other
    # stage filter names the failure stage to match exactly. The history
    # key filter is a plain string equality: no prefix matching, case
    # folding or path normalization.
    if op is not None and event["op"] != op:
        return False
    if stage is not None:
        if stage == "成功":
            if event["error"] is not None or event["stage"] is not None:
                return False
        elif event["stage"] != stage:
            return False
    if key is not None and event["key"] != key:
        return False
    return True


def search(
    path: str,
    cursor: str | None = None,
    limit: int = _DEFAULT_LIMIT,
    op: str | None = None,
    stage: str | None = None,
    key: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return one page of audit events matching the given filters.

    ``path`` must be a non-empty string. ``cursor`` is ``None`` or a
    non-empty string -- it need not name an existing event -- and only
    events whose audit key is strictly greater than it in code-point
    order are considered. ``limit`` is the page size: an integer from 1
    to 1000 (booleans are rejected), defaulting to 100. Each of ``op``,
    ``stage`` and ``key`` is an optional filter; all given filters must
    hold simultaneously. ``op`` is ``"copy"`` or ``"restore"``; ``stage``
    is one of ``"成功"`` (events whose error and stage are both null),
    ``"校验"``, ``"执行"``, ``"同步"`` and ``"回滚"`` (events that failed
    at that stage); ``key`` matches the event's history key by exact
    string equality. Any other value raises ``ValueError``.

    The journal is scanned in ascending audit-key code-point order and
    filtered afterwards, so non-matching events never consume page
    capacity. Returns ``{"events": [[audit_key, event], ...], "next":
    cursor_or_none}``: each event is a fresh copy with the public field
    order, and ``next`` is the audit key of the page's last item when
    further matching events remain, else ``None``. With no matching
    events the page is empty and ``next`` is ``None``.

    The query is strictly read-only: a missing journal raises
    ``FileNotFoundError``; malformed JSON or UTF-8, a negative-zero
    literal, or an unsupported version, structure, order or digest chain
    raises ``ValueError``; any other locking or I/O failure raises
    ``OSError``. It holds the journal's companion lock shared only while
    the file is opened and read, so a query racing a writer observes
    either the complete previous document or the complete new one.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
    if cursor is not None and (not isinstance(cursor, str) or not cursor):
        raise ValueError("cursor must be None or a non-empty string")
    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected as a page size.
    if not isinstance(limit, int) or isinstance(limit, bool) \
            or not 1 <= limit <= _MAX_LIMIT:
        raise ValueError("limit must be an integer between 1 and 1000")
    if op is not None and op not in _OPS:
        raise ValueError('op filter must be "copy" or "restore"')
    if stage is not None and stage not in _SEARCH_STAGES:
        raise ValueError(
            "stage filter must be one of 成功, 校验, 执行, 同步, 回滚")
    if key is not None and (not isinstance(key, str) or not key):
        raise ValueError("key filter must be a non-empty string")

    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
    document = _read_existing_document(realpath)

    # The persisted events are validated to be in ascending key
    # code-point order, so the document order is the scan order. One
    # extra match is collected to learn whether the page is the last.
    matches: list[list[Any]] = []
    for audit_key, event in document["events"].items():
        if cursor is not None and audit_key <= cursor:
            continue
        if not _matches(event, op, stage, key):
            continue
        matches.append([audit_key, dict(event)])
        if len(matches) > limit:
            break

    if len(matches) > limit:
        page = matches[:limit]
        next_cursor: str | None = page[-1][0]
    else:
        page = matches
        next_cursor = None
    return {"events": page, "next": next_cursor}


def verify(path: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Verify the integrity of the audit journal stored at ``path``.

    ``path`` must be a non-empty string, else ``ValueError``. A missing
    journal raises ``FileNotFoundError``; malformed JSON or UTF-8, a
    negative-zero literal, or an unsupported version, field order or
    structure raises ``ValueError``; any other locking or I/O failure
    raises ``OSError``. The query never writes and holds the journal's
    companion lock shared only while the file is opened and read.

    Returns ``version``, ``count``, ``sealed``, ``valid``,
    ``first_invalid`` and ``head``, in that order. A well-formed version
    1 journal carries no chain: ``count`` is its real event count,
    ``sealed`` and ``valid`` are false and ``first_invalid`` and
    ``head`` are null. A sealed (version 2) journal whose chain is
    complete reports ``sealed`` and ``valid`` true, ``first_invalid``
    null and ``head`` the root digest the file declares. A chain
    deviation never raises: ``valid`` is false and ``first_invalid`` is
    the zero-based position of the first event whose digest does not
    match its content or whose predecessor reference is wrong, or the
    event count when only the root head disagrees with the last event's
    digest.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")

    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
    with _file_lock(realpath, shared=True):
        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
    document = _parse_document(realpath, raw)

    events = document["events"]
    if document["version"] == 1:
        return {"version": 1, "count": len(events), "sealed": False,
                "valid": False, "first_invalid": None, "head": None}
    first_invalid = _chain_first_invalid(document)
    return {"version": 2, "count": len(events), "sealed": True,
            "valid": first_invalid is None, "first_invalid": first_invalid,
            "head": document["head"]}

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse

from . import auth
from .server import serve


class _Once(argparse.Action):
    """Optional argument that may be given at most once."""

    def __call__(self, parser, namespace, values, option_string=None):
        if getattr(namespace, self.dest, None) is not None:
            parser.error(f"{option_string} must not be given more than once")
        setattr(namespace, self.dest, values)


def parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    command = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="carbon_market")
    subcommands = command.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    server = subcommands.add_parser("serve", help="start the HTTP service")
    server.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
    server.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8000)
    server.add_argument(
        "--audit", action=_Once,
        help="audit journal file to expose at GET /audit")
    server.add_argument(
        "--token", action=_Once,
        help="token clients must send in the X-Audit-Token header")
    server.add_argument(
        "--auth", action=_Once,
        help="multi-token scoped authorization file for GET /audit, "
             "exclusive with --token")
    return command


def main() -> None:
    command = parser()
    args = command.parse_args()
    if args.command == "serve":
        # --audit pairs with exactly one authorization method: the
        # single --token or the multi-token --auth file. Both omitted
        # keeps GET /audit a plain 404; --audit without a method, a
        # method without --audit, both methods at once, an empty value
        # or a repeated option is a usage error and exits with
        # argparse's status 2.
        if args.audit is None:
            if args.token is not None or args.auth is not None:
                command.error("--token and --auth require --audit")
        else:
            if not args.audit:
                command.error("--audit must be non-empty")
            if (args.token is None) == (args.auth is None):
                command.error(
                    "--audit requires exactly one of --token and --auth")
            if args.token is not None and not args.token:
                command.error("--token must be non-empty")
            if args.auth is not None and not args.auth:
                command.error("--auth must be non-empty")
        if args.auth:
            # The whole configuration is validated before the port is
            # bound; any failure is a usage error with status 2.
            try:
                auth.load(args.auth)
            except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
                command.error(f"invalid --auth file: {exc}")
        serve(args.host, args.port, audit_path=args.audit, token=args.token,
              auth=args.auth)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    ``digest`` is the 32 raw bytes of the token's SHA-256. Each scope
    is ``None`` for ``"*"`` (unrestricted) or a frozenset of the
    allowed filter values.
    """

    name: str
    digest: bytes
    grace_until: int | None
    ops: frozenset[str] | None
    stages: frozenset[str] | None
    keys: frozenset[str] | None


def _validate_name(raw: object) -> str:
    if not isinstance(raw, str) or not raw:
        raise ValueError("auth name must be a non-empty string")
    return raw


def _validate_digest(raw: object) -> bytes:
    if not isinstance(raw, str) or len(raw) != _DIGEST_HEX_LENGTH \
            or any(char not in _HEX_DIGITS for char in raw):
        raise ValueError(
            "auth digest must be the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of "
            "the token")
    return bytes.fromhex(raw)


def _validate_grace_until(raw: object) -> int | None:
    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected as a cutoff.
    if raw is None:
        return None
    if not isinstance(raw, int) or isinstance(raw, bool) or raw < 0:
        raise ValueError(
            "auth grace cutoff must be null or a non-negative integer")
    return raw


def _validate_scope(raw: object, allowed: tuple[str, ...] | None,
                    label: str) -> frozenset[str] | None:
    # "*" lifts the restriction entirely; otherwise the scope is an
    # array of distinct non-empty strings, drawn from the search filter
    # domain when one applies (operations and stages).
    if raw == "*":
        return None
    if not isinstance(raw, list):
        raise ValueError(f'auth {label} scope must be "*" or an array')
    values: set[str] = set()
    for item in raw:
        if not isinstance(item, str) or not item:
            raise ValueError(
                f"auth {label} scope entries must be non-empty strings")
        if allowed is not None and item not in allowed:
            raise ValueError(
                f"auth {label} scope entries must be drawn from "
                + ", ".join(allowed))
        if item in values:
            raise ValueError(f"auth {label} scope entries must be distinct")
        values.add(item)
    return frozenset(values)


def _parse_line(line: str) -> Record:
    try:
        data: Any = strict_loads(line)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ValueError("auth line is not valid JSON") from exc
    if not isinstance(data, list) or len(data) != 6:
        raise ValueError(
            "auth line must be an array of name, digest, grace cutoff "
            "and the operation, stage and history-key scopes")
    name, digest, grace_until, ops, stages, keys = data
    return Record(
        name=_validate_name(name),
        digest=_validate_digest(digest),
        grace_until=_validate_grace_until(grace_until),
        ops=_validate_scope(ops, _OPS, "operation"),
        stages=_validate_scope(stages, _STAGES, "stage"),
        keys=_validate_scope(keys, None, "history-key"),
    )


def load(path: str) -> list[Record]:
    """Read and validate the whole authorization file.

    Every non-empty line must be a six-element JSON array as described
    in the module docstring; names and digests must each be unique and
    the file must yield at least one record. A missing file or other
    I/O failure raises :class:`OSError`; invalid UTF-8, malformed JSON
    (negative-zero literals included), a wrong shape, a bad value, a
    duplicated name or digest, or no records at all raise
    :class:`ValueError`. The returned list is a complete snapshot: a
    caller either gets the whole old configuration or the whole new
    one, never a mixture.
    """
    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
        raw = handle.read()
    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"auth file {path!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc

    records: list[Record] = []
    names: set[str] = set()
    digests: set[bytes] = set()
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        record = _parse_line(line)
        if record.name in names:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate auth name {record.name!r}")
        if record.digest in digests:
            raise ValueError("duplicate auth token digest")
        names.add(record.name)
        digests.add(record.digest)
        records.append(record)

    if not records:
        raise ValueError(f"auth file {path!r} holds no token records")
    return records


def identify(records: list[Record], token: str,
             now: int | None = None) -> Record | None:
    """Resolve a presented token to its record, or ``None``.

    The token's SHA-256 is compared against every record's digest with
    a fixed-time comparison and the identity is decided only after all
    records were checked, so the comparison count never reveals a
    prefix match. A token whose grace cutoff lies in the past -- the
    current Unix second is greater than it -- yields ``None`` exactly
    like an unknown digest. ``now`` defaults to the current Unix
    second.
    """
    if now is None:
        now = int(time.time())
    candidate = hashlib.sha256(token.encode("utf-8")).digest()
    matched: Record | None = None
    for record in records:
        if hmac.compare_digest(candidate, record.digest):
            matched = record
    if matched is None:
        return None
    if matched.grace_until is not None and now > matched.grace_until:
        return None
    return matched


def scope_allows(record: Record, params: dict[str, str]) -> bool:
    """Check validated query filters against the record's scopes.

    A ``"*"`` scope (``None``) lets the request omit the filter or use
    any legal value; an array scope requires the request to carry the
    filter explicitly with a value in the array. Only the op, stage and
    key filters constrain; cursor and limit are not scoped.
    """
    for scope, name in ((record.ops, "op"), (record.stages, "stage"),
                        (record.keys, "key")):
        if scope is None:
            continue
        value = params.get(name)
        if value is None or value not in scope:
            return False
    return True
